🌶️ OpenAI is bringing some heat to the AI chip race. Its Jalapeño inference chip reportedly packs Samsung HBM4, with Broadcom and TSMC also in the supply chain.  🔥 OpenAI’s Jalapeño reportedly runs on TSMC’s 3nm process, putting it in the same fight as NVIDIA’s Blackwell and Rubin for advanced wafers, HBM and cutting-edge packaging capacity.  💡More: https://buff.ly/FC4QHba 🔗   #OpenAI  #Samsung  #HBM4  #Broadcom  #TSMC

📈 HBM prices could be in for a major jump in 2027 as NVIDIA rolls out Rubin Ultra: 50%+ could be the baseline, while the bull case reportedly sees prices soaring 79% YoY.  👉 Samsung and SK hynix could gain pricing power as NVIDIA raises server prices, leaving more room to absorb higher HBM costs—and less reason to push back on price hikes.  💡More: https://buff.ly/tHUkNUr 🔗   #HBM  #NVIDIA  #Samsung  #SKhynix

📢 Samsung and SK hynix took different paths at Hot Chips 2026: Samsung pushed custom HBM and zHBM, claiming 70% higher power efficiency vs. HBM4e, while SK hynix explored how TSMC’s CoWoS and Intel’s EMIB shape HBM integration.  🔥 Thermal management is another focus: Samsung presents its Heat Path Block (HPB) for cHBM4, designed to cut peak temperature by more than 35%, while SK hynix introduces its own localized hotspot solution, dubbed I-HBM.  💡More: https://buff.ly/oAZBp3A 🔗   #Samsung  #SKhynix  #HBM

🚀 Since beginning production earlier this year, Micron’s Sanand assembly & test plant in India has received a boost as Gujarat approves 12-hour shifts—the first such approval in the state, paving the way for more continuous production and higher output.  🏭 Sanand is set to assemble and test tens of millions of chips in 2026, with annual output ramping to hundreds of millions from 2027. At full capacity, the site could account for up to 10% of Micron’s global output.  💡More: https://buff.ly/HS5NpcO 🔗   #Micron

📈 Samsung Foundry’s turnaround may be closer than expected. Reported price hikes of up to 15% across SF4, SF5 and 8nm could be a key catalyst—higher than  #TSMC’s planned up to 10% increase in 2027.  🔥Just a year ago, the picture was very different: Samsung was reportedly cutting prices to win orders, with its 2nm wafers said to be priced around $20K—~33% below TSMC’s $30K.  💡More: https://buff.ly/wLfCocS 🔗   #Samsung

👀 Could TSMC become a bigger part of Team Blue’s next-gen CPU plans? While Nova Lake is expected to rely largely on 18A, Intel may tap TSMC’s N2X for part of Razor Lake, depending on how 18A-P performs.   🤔 TSMC’s process roadmap places N2X in 2027, aligning with the expected timeline for Razor Lake.   💡More: https://buff.ly/bMNpQ6M 🔗   #Intel  #TSMC  #2nm

🚀 Memory giants are moving into the optical era. SK hynix just unveiled its CPO roadmap, featuring an optics-centric architecture that uses a photonic interposer to directly link memory and processors.  👉 SK hynix is looking beyond HBM. Its CPO architecture could let multiple AI accelerators share a large memory pool, enabling more flexible data movement and more efficient scaling as AI models grow larger and more complex.  💡More: https://buff.ly/Ex9oYSJ 🔗   #SKhynix  #CPO
